scope: AlchLang initial language terms for governed domain descriptions inside CA2-CAP-ALCHLANG-MODEL-GOVERNED-DOMAINS.

records.context: CyberAlchemy product language for expressing governed meaning about one bounded domain before formal construction.
records.intended_use: Candidate initial vocabulary for describing worlds in which humans, traditional software, and agents may later act under explicit constraints.
records.decision_owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 product owner

propose.normative_voice: AlchLang is the CyberAlchemy product language through which a responsible domain owner expresses bounded domain meaning, ambiguity, relationships, behavior, and authority limits for later formal construction.
propose.formal_voice: AlchLangDescription = (context, terms, edges, rules, states, transitions, events, actions, permissions, examples, open_questions, authority_boundaries, provenance, owners).
propose.plain_language_voice: AlchLang is how a domain owner describes the world before software or agents are allowed to act in it.
propose.domain_context_voice: AlchLang owns product-facing domain expression; DomainSpec v2 remains its later formal construction substrate.
propose.boundary: AlchLang is not DomainSpec, a parser, prompt, agent, compiler, implementation, permission grant, or proof that the described meaning was accepted.
propose.drift_route: Refresh through CyberAlchemy v2 Define when the Product anchor, language scope, DomainSpec boundary, or named owner changes.

records.context: One bounded domain expressed through AlchLang before DomainSpec construction.
records.intended_use: Container for the initial AlchLang semantic primitives and their explicit gaps.
records.decision_owner_route: AlchLang capability owner plus bounded-domain owner
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus bounded-domain owner

propose.normative_voice: A Governed Domain Description is an owner-qualified bounded description whose terms, typed edges, rules, states, transitions, events, actions, permissions, examples, open questions, authority boundaries, sources, and owners remain explicit.
propose.formal_voice: GovernedDomainDescription = (domain_context, vocabulary, relation_graph, behavior, authority, examples, gaps, provenance, owners).
propose.plain_language_voice: It is the reviewable description of a domain, including what is known, how things relate, what may happen, and what is still unclear.
propose.domain_context_voice: It is AlchLang business meaning that may later become input to a separately accepted DomainSpec source.
propose.boundary: It is not unrestricted prose, an admitted ontology, a DomainSpec project, generated system ontology, implementation, or owner acceptance decision.
propose.drift_route: Refresh when the required semantic categories, bounded context, consumers, or owner routes change.

records.context: One named concept-bearing node inside an AlchLang Governed Domain Description.
records.intended_use: Give every required domain concept an explicit meaning, source, owner, and disposition.
records.decision_owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner plus named bounded-domain meaning owner
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner

specialize.narrower_context: The knowledge-object or node role within one AlchLang Governed Domain Description.
specialize.normative_voice: An Ontology Term is one named domain concept with bounded meaning, aliases, context, sources, owner, current disposition, and unresolved ambiguity, specialized from the knowledge-object component of CAV2-D19 Ontology.
specialize.formal_voice: OntologyTerm = (term_id, term, aliases, meaning, context, source_refs, owner_route, disposition, open_questions).
specialize.plain_language_voice: An Ontology Term is one named thing the domain needs to talk about precisely.
specialize.domain_context_voice: AlchLang uses terms as business-meaning nodes; later system types remain separate realizations.
specialize.boundary: It is not automatically canonical, universally shared, a DomainSpec type, an implementation class, or proof that its meaning is true.
specialize.drift_route: Re-evaluate the specialization when CAV2-D19 or the AlchLang term contract changes.

records.context: One typed directional relationship between Ontology Terms inside an AlchLang Governed Domain Description.
records.intended_use: Make domain relationships explicit, typed, directional, source-bound, and owner-qualified.
records.decision_owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner plus named bounded-domain meaning owner
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner

specialize.narrower_context: The typed-relation or edge role within one AlchLang Governed Domain Description.
specialize.normative_voice: An Ontology Edge is one typed directional relationship between two resolved or explicitly open Ontology Terms, with a business sentence, sources, owner route, and non-collapse boundary, specialized from the typed-relation component of CAV2-D19 Ontology.
specialize.formal_voice: OntologyEdge = (edge_id, relation_type, source_term_ref, target_term_ref, business_sentence, source_refs, owner_route, boundary).
specialize.plain_language_voice: An Ontology Edge says exactly how one domain term relates to another.
specialize.domain_context_voice: AlchLang edges preserve business relationships before any DomainSpec relationship or implementation connection is selected.
specialize.boundary: It is not an untyped association, shared spelling, implementation dependency, generated graph edge, or proof that the relation holds in reality.
specialize.drift_route: Re-evaluate the specialization when CAV2-D19, endpoint semantics, or the AlchLang edge contract changes.

records.context: A proposition constraining valid situations or behavior in one bounded domain.
records.intended_use: Express business invariants and restrictions without pretending they are already enforced.
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: Bounded-domain owner plus AlchLang capability owner

propose.normative_voice: A Domain Rule is an owner-qualified proposition that constrains valid domain situations, classifications, decisions, or behavior and states its required facts, scope, exceptions, and consequence.
propose.formal_voice: DomainRule = (rule_id, proposition, scope, required_fact_refs, condition, consequence, exception_refs, owner_route, source_refs).
propose.plain_language_voice: A Domain Rule says what must, may, or must not be true in the domain.
propose.domain_context_voice: AlchLang records the business rule and its limits before validators, tests, or runtime enforcement exist.
propose.boundary: A Domain Rule is not implementation code, a generated validator, an authority grant, or evidence that enforcement occurred.
propose.drift_route: Refresh when facts, scope, exceptions, consequence, or the rule owner changes.

records.context: A meaningful condition occupied by a named domain subject.
records.intended_use: Describe lifecycle conditions separately from the changes between them.
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: Bounded-domain owner plus AlchLang capability owner

propose.normative_voice: A Domain State is one named, mutually interpretable condition that a specified domain subject may occupy under explicit entry, persistence, and exit meaning.
propose.formal_voice: DomainState = (state_id, subject_term_ref, meaning, entry_conditions, persistence_conditions, exit_conditions, owner_route).
propose.plain_language_voice: A Domain State describes the meaningful condition something is currently in.
propose.domain_context_voice: AlchLang states express business lifecycle meaning before a state-machine realization is selected.
propose.boundary: A Domain State is not a database flag, runtime process state, transition, event, or proof of current reality unless separately evidenced.
propose.drift_route: Refresh when subject identity, state meaning, or lifecycle conditions change.

records.context: An allowed change between two Domain States of the same bounded subject.
records.intended_use: Express lifecycle changes with source, target, trigger, guards, and owner explicit.
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: Bounded-domain owner plus AlchLang capability owner

propose.normative_voice: A Domain Transition is an allowed directed change from one Domain State to another for the same subject, with trigger, guards, required authority boundary, resulting event, and prohibited alternatives explicit.
propose.formal_voice: DomainTransition = (transition_id, subject_term_ref, from_state_ref, to_state_ref, trigger, guard_rule_refs, authority_boundary_ref, resulting_event_ref, owner_route).
propose.plain_language_voice: A Domain Transition says when and how something may move from one meaningful state to another.
propose.domain_context_voice: AlchLang transitions carry reviewed business lifecycle meaning before machine generation.
propose.boundary: A Domain Transition is not the action requesting it, the event recording it, a runtime state machine, or permission to execute it.
propose.drift_route: Refresh when states, trigger, guards, resulting event, or authority boundary changes.

records.context: A domain-significant occurrence described as something that happened.
records.intended_use: Record business occurrences separately from commands, actions, and state claims.
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: Bounded-domain owner plus AlchLang capability owner

propose.normative_voice: A Domain Event is an immutable domain-significant occurrence stated in the past tense with subject, facts, occurrence context, provenance expectations, and affected meaning explicit.
propose.formal_voice: DomainEvent = (event_id, event_type, subject_ref, facts, occurred_at_or_context, provenance_requirements, affected_term_refs).
propose.plain_language_voice: A Domain Event says that something meaningful happened in the domain.
propose.domain_context_voice: AlchLang events define business occurrence contracts before transport or storage contracts are chosen.
propose.boundary: A Domain Event is not a command, requested action, permission, mutable state, transport message, or evidence that a runtime emitted it.
propose.drift_route: Refresh when occurrence meaning, required facts, subject, or provenance expectations change.

records.context: An intentional domain operation a participant may request or perform under explicit rules.
records.intended_use: Name possible domain behavior without granting execution authority.
records.decision_owner_route: Named bounded-domain meaning owner plus bounded effect owner
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: Bounded-domain owner plus AlchLang capability owner

propose.normative_voice: A Domain Action is one intentional operation over named domain subjects whose actor class, inputs, preconditions, permission conditions, confirmation requirements, expected outcomes, and authority boundary are explicit.
propose.formal_voice: DomainAction = (action_id, actor_refs, subject_refs, input_refs, precondition_rule_refs, permission_ref, confirmation_policy, outcome_refs, authority_boundary_ref).
propose.plain_language_voice: A Domain Action describes something a participant may try to do in the modeled world.
propose.domain_context_voice: AlchLang actions are governed business possibilities; later agent tools are replaceable realizations.
propose.boundary: A Domain Action is not an executable tool, command handler, API endpoint, permission grant, execution record, or authorization to cause an effect.
propose.drift_route: Refresh when actor, subject, inputs, preconditions, permission, confirmation, outcome, or authority boundary changes.

records.context: A descriptive condition under which one Domain Action is allowed for a participant in a bounded domain.
records.intended_use: Preserve permission meaning while keeping the separate authority required to make a decision count.
records.decision_owner_route: Named bounded-domain meaning owner plus bounded authority owner
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: Bounded-domain owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner

propose.normative_voice: A Domain Permission is an owner-qualified descriptive condition linking an actor class, Domain Action, subject or target, scope, required facts, exceptions, and confirmation obligations; it does not itself make an authorization decision count.
propose.formal_voice: DomainPermission = (permission_id, actor_ref, action_ref, target_ref, scope, required_fact_refs, exception_refs, confirmation_policy, authority_boundary_ref).
propose.plain_language_voice: A Domain Permission describes when a particular actor is allowed to attempt a particular action in a particular boundary.
propose.domain_context_voice: AlchLang separates permission meaning from CAV2 authority, runtime authorization, and effect execution.
propose.boundary: It is not CAV2-D34 Authority, an access-control grant, authorization decision, credential, capability token, runtime enforcement, or execution evidence.
propose.drift_route: Refresh when actor, action, target, scope, facts, exceptions, confirmation, or authority boundary changes.

records.context: A concrete situation used to expose intended meaning and boundaries in one AlchLang description.
records.intended_use: Test interpretation with positive, negative, boundary, and missing-information cases.
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: Bounded-domain owner plus AlchLang capability owner

propose.normative_voice: A Domain Example is one concrete positive, negative, boundary, or missing-information situation that names relevant facts, expected interpretation, affected rules, and the meaning boundary it is intended to expose.
propose.formal_voice: DomainExample = (example_id, kind, fact_assignments, expected_interpretation, affected_rule_refs, boundary_witness, owner_route).
propose.plain_language_voice: A Domain Example is a realistic situation used to check whether everyone understands the model the same way.
propose.domain_context_voice: AlchLang examples pressure-test business meaning and may later inform generated tests without becoming those tests.
propose.boundary: A Domain Example is not a general rule, exhaustive test suite, implementation fixture, proof, or permission to infer omitted facts.
propose.drift_route: Refresh when facts, expected interpretation, rule coverage, or boundary witness changes.

records.context: Unresolved meaning or missing decision inside a Governed Domain Description.
records.intended_use: Keep ambiguity visible, owner-routed, and capable of blocking only the affected use.
records.decision_owner_route: Named owner of the unresolved domain matter
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: Named bounded-domain owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Define

propose.normative_voice: An Open Domain Question is an unresolved, unclear, disputed, or missing piece of domain meaning that records its question, reason, affected concepts and uses, decision owner, stop condition, and next action.
propose.formal_voice: OpenDomainQuestion = (question_id, question, reason, affected_refs, affected_uses, decision_owner_route, stop_conditions, next_action).
propose.plain_language_voice: An Open Domain Question is something important the model does not yet know and refuses to guess.
propose.domain_context_voice: AlchLang preserves semantic gaps as first-class meaning instead of letting an agent or compiler silently resolve them.
propose.boundary: It is not an answered question, defect concealment, automatic blocker for unrelated uses, or permission for a tool to choose the answer.
propose.drift_route: Refresh or supersede when the owner answers, narrows, disputes, or retires the question.

records.context: The CAV2-D34 Authority specialization attached to domain meaning, decisions, and actions in one AlchLang description.
records.intended_use: State who or what may make one domain matter count, for which scope, operation, basis, and effect.
records.decision_owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner plus bounded authority owner
records.challenge_or_refresh_route: CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner plus bounded authority owner

specialize.narrower_context: Authority claims attached to terms, rules, permissions, decisions, transitions, actions, and examples in one bounded AlchLang description.
specialize.normative_voice: A Domain Authority Boundary is the AlchLang specialization of CAV2-D34 that names the scope, owner or owner route, authority surface, governed object, allowed operation, basis, effect, and challenge route for one bounded domain matter.
specialize.formal_voice: DomainAuthorityBoundary(x) = (scope, owner, surface, governed_object, operation, basis, effect, challenge_route).
specialize.plain_language_voice: It says who or what is allowed to make a particular domain decision count, and only within which limits.
specialize.domain_context_voice: AlchLang carries authority limits forward without granting them to language, validation, generated tools, agents, or compiled artifacts.
specialize.boundary: It is not truth, confidence, permission by itself, repository access, generated status, runtime enforcement, or implementation success.
specialize.drift_route: Re-evaluate the specialization when CAV2-D34 or any authority tuple field changes.

records.context: The canonical D65 boundary governing any later movement from reviewed AlchLang meaning toward implementation-bearing construction.
records.intended_use: Reuse the exact canonical construction order without copying or redefining its normative meaning.

claim_ceiling: Fourteen current AlchLang handled-definition records for one bounded initial-language use: ten proposals, three specializations, and one canonical reuse. They are isolated Define candidates, not entries in the central Auth registry, canonical CyberAlchemy definitions, an accepted Definition Pack, a DomainSpec source, implementation authority, or promotion evidence.
